subject: Integration & Onboarding Plan — Redwood + Brightline Health (recap)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Lee <sara.lee@brightlinehealth.com>, Michael Nguyen <m.nguyen@brightlinehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Integration & Onboarding Plan — Redwood + Brightline Health (recap)

Hi Sara / Michael —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery + the integrated onboarding outline so we have alignment before Rishi follows up with technical next steps. High-level notes: 

- Pain points you confirmed: latency and inference cost on peak conversational load (~1200 concurrent users), cold-start tail latency for long-context patient histories, and desire for on-prem telemetry for audit purposes.
- Current stack: frontend React app + Python-based backend (FastAPI) using in-house LLM endpoints for NLU; some embeddings used for search (Postgres + pgvector).
- Success criteria for a PoC: 30% reduction in average token cost per request at p95 latency <= 250ms, stable throughput for 1000 rps sustained bursts, and demonstrable audit logs and token-level usage reporting.

Integration / PoC plan (proposed):
1) Week 1: Kickoff & environment setup — exchange test data contract, confirm API keys and VPC access options, get SOC2 evidence and IP allowlist configured. (Owner: Marissa / Brightline IT)
2) Week 2: SDK onboarding — Rishi to provide Python SDK + JavaScript snippets; sample endpoints for generation, streaming, and embeddings. Quick sanity-run against a small dataset. (Owner: Rishi)
3) Weeks 3–4: Performance tuning — enable batching and KV prefix caching, run synthetic load to reproduce production-like patterns; iterate on quantization/profile suggestions. (Owner: Rishi / Brightline eng)
4) Week 5: Validation & metrics — compare cost/latency against baseline, deliver dashboard access in Redwood Console. (Owner: Marissa / Brightline PM)
5) Week 6: Readout & next steps — decision to move to Dedicated or Private, contract sketch.

Attachments: redwood-poc-plan.pdf (outline + milestones), redwood-sdk-examples.zip (small code samples).

Open items / asks for Brightline:
- Confirm whether you prefer a VPC Private deployment or Hosted with encrypted transit (we recommended Private for PHI).
- Provide a sample anonymized transcript for tuning and throughput shaping.
- Confirm technical owner for the PoC (name + calendar availability).

I'll put a short calendar hold for Thursday to review the SDK examples; Rishi will follow with terminals and a short runbook for the first smoke test.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks Marissa — this is great, appreciate the clear plan. A couple clarifying items from our side: 

1) SDK languages: our backend is Python (FastAPI) but we also have a small Java service that handles analytics. Can you confirm production-ready Python + Java SDKs or at least clear REST examples for Java?
2) Timeline: week 6 sounds reasonable. We’d like to aim for an internal readout on 2026-04-15 — is that compatible with your dates?
3) Compliance: given PHI concerns, we need details on keys/KMS and whether Redwood Private can run in our GCP VPC (we're GCP-only). Also request the SOC2 extract you mentioned.

Technical owner will be Michael Nguyen (m.nguyen@brightlinehealth.com). He’s copied and can coordinate environment access.

If you can send the SDK snippets and SOC2 extract, we’ll try to schedule a kickoff this week.

Best,
Sara

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Integration & Onboarding Plan — Redwood + Brightline Health (recap)

Thanks for the recap, Marissa. Quick technical notes / next steps from my side: 

- SDKs: We have a maintained Python SDK and a JS/Node SDK. We don’t ship a first-class Java SDK, but we provide clear REST examples and a thin Java client template in the repo. I’ll include an example of how to stream responses in Java (EventSource/Server-Sent) in the code bundle.
- API compatibility: Redwood exposes a stable REST surface (generation, streaming, embeddings) and supports OpenTelemetry traces that you can ingest; models are versioned and pinned via model tags. Should be straightforward to plug into your FastAPI endpoints.
- On-prem / VPC: We support GCP VPC peering for Private deployments (customers can bring their own KMS). We’ll prepare a short checklist for network/firewall rules.
- PoC milestones (more granular):
   * Day 0–2: account setup, API keys, sample dataset ingestion (anonymized).
   * Day 3–7: SDK smoke test + one sample integration on staging.
   * Week 2–3: baseline perf runs (single model) + enable batching + KV caching.
   * Week 4: run production-like load (throughput shaping) and collect p95 / cost numbers.

I’ll attach: a short SDK README, the redwood-soc2-extract.pdf and a template for firewall rules. Also, please share an anonymized transcript and a contact for GCP networking to start the peering request.

I’m free for a 30-min technical kickoff Thursday 10–11AM PT if that works for Michael.

Thanks,
Rishi
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
